sections.title: Primeval History
sections.description: From Creation to the Tower of Babel

sections.title: Abraham
sections.description: God's Call and Covenant with Abraham

sections.title: Joseph
sections.description: Joseph in Egypt and the Family Reunion

events.title: Creation
events.description: God creates heaven and earth in six days: light, the sky, land and sea, plants, celestial bodies, animals, and finally mankind in His image. On the seventh day, God rests.

events.title: Adam and Eve in the Garden of Eden
events.description: God forms Adam from the dust of the ground and breathes life into him. He plants the Garden of Eden and places Adam there to work it. Eve is created from Adam's rib as a helper for him.

events.title: The Fall
events.description: The serpent tempts Eve to eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, and Adam also eats. They discover their nakedness, and God drives them out of the Garden of Eden. God announces judgment against the serpent, the woman, and the man.

events.title: Cain and Abel
events.description: Cain and Abel bring offerings to God. God looks with favor on Abel's offering, but not on Cain's. In jealousy, Cain kills his brother Abel. God curses Cain to be a fugitive and wanderer on the earth.

events.title: The Line of Seth
events.description: Adam and Eve have a son named Seth. Through Seth's line, the lineage continues to Noah. Enoch walks with God and is taken away. Methuselah lives longer than any other person.

events.title: The Flood and Noah's Ark
events.description: Evil on the earth is great, and God regrets having made humanity. God commands Noah to build an ark to save his family and animals of every kind. The flood covers the whole earth for 40 days. Noah sends out a dove that returns with an olive leaf.

events.title: God's Covenant with Noah
events.description: God blesses Noah and his sons and establishes a covenant that he will never again destroy the earth with a flood. The rainbow is set as a sign of the covenant.

events.title: The Tower of Babel
events.description: People gather together and begin to build a city with a tower that reaches up to heaven. God confuses their language and scatters them over the whole earth.

events.title: God's Call to Abram
events.description: God calls Abram to leave Ur and go to a land he will show him. God promises to make him into a great nation and to bless all the families of the earth through him. Abram leaves Haran with Sarai and Lot.

events.title: Abram in Egypt
events.description: A famine drives Abram to Egypt. Fearing he will be killed, he presents Sarai as his sister. Pharaoh takes Sarai into his house, but God strikes Pharaoh with plagues. Pharaoh sends Abram away.

events.title: Lot Separates from Abram
events.description: Conflicts between the herdsmen of Abram and Lot lead to their separation. Lot chooses the fertile Jordan Valley and settles near Sodom. God repeats His promise of the land to Abram.

events.title: God's Covenant with Abram
events.description: God makes a covenant with Abram. He promises him descendants as numerous as the stars and pledges to give them the land from the River of Egypt to the Euphrates. God confirms the covenant by passing between the divided sacrificial animals as a burning torch.

events.title: Hagar and Ishmael
events.description: Sarai gives her maidservant Hagar to Abram to bear children through her. Hagar becomes pregnant and looks down on Sarai. Hagar flees into the wilderness, but the angel of the Lord sends her back. She gives birth to Ishmael.

events.title: Abraham's New Name and Circumcision
events.description: God gives Abram the new name Abraham and Sarai the new name Sarah. Circumcision is instituted as a sign of the covenant between God and Abraham and his descendants. God promises that Sarah will bear a son.

events.title: The Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah
events.description: Three men visit Abraham, and he intercedes for Sodom. Two angels arrive in Sodom, and Lot welcomes them. The people of Sodom surround the house. God destroys Sodom and Gomorrah with fire and sulfur. Lot's wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt.

events.title: The Birth of Isaac
events.description: Sarah gives birth to Isaac in her old age, as God had promised. Abraham circumcises Isaac on the eighth day. Sarah demands that Hagar and Ishmael be sent away, and Abraham sends them into the wilderness with a heavy heart.

events.title: God Tests Abraham - The Sacrifice of Isaac
events.description: God tests Abraham and asks him to sacrifice Isaac on Mount Moriah. Abraham obeys in faith, but at the last moment the angel of the Lord intervenes and stops him. A ram is sacrificed instead. God confirms His blessing.

events.title: The Death of Sarah
events.description: Sarah dies at the age of 127 in Hebron. Abraham buys the cave of Machpelah from the Hittite Ephron as a burial site. It is the first piece of land Abraham owns in the promised land.

events.title: Rebecca Becomes Isaac's Wife
events.description: Abraham sends his servant to Mesopotamia to find a wife for Isaac. The servant meets Rebecca at the well, and she shows hospitality. Rebecca travels back with the servant and becomes Isaac's wife.

events.title: Esau and Jacob Are Born
events.description: Rebecca gives birth to twins: Esau and Jacob. God says that the older shall serve the younger. Esau sells his birthright to Jacob for a meal of lentil stew.

events.title: Jacob Steals the Blessing
events.description: Isaac is old and blind. With Rebecca's help, Jacob pretends to be Esau and receives Isaac's blessing. Esau discovers the deception and hates Jacob, who must flee to his uncle Laban in Haran.

events.title: Jacob's Ladder
events.description: While fleeing from Esau, Jacob spends the night at Bethel. He dreams of a ladder between heaven and earth with angels going up and down on it. God confirms Abraham's promise to Jacob. Jacob sets up a memorial stone and calls the place Bethel.

events.title: Jacob with Laban
events.description: Jacob serves Laban for seven years for Rachel, but is tricked into marrying Leah first. He serves another seven years for Rachel. Jacob has twelve sons and one daughter. Finally, Jacob flees from Laban with his family and wealth.

events.title: Jacob Wrestles with God
events.description: At the river Jabbok, Jacob wrestles all night with a man. The man dislocates Jacob's hip, but Jacob does not let go. Jacob receives the new name Israel, which means 'he struggles with God'.

events.title: Reconciliation with Esau
events.description: Jacob meets Esau again after many years. Instead of revenge, Esau runs to meet him, embraces him and weeps. The brothers are reconciled, and Jacob settles in Canaan.

events.title: Dinah at Shechem
events.description: Dinah, Jacob's daughter, is violated by Shechem. Simeon and Levi avenge her by killing all the men of the city, which arouses Jacob's anger and fear.

events.title: Rachel's death
events.description: Rachel dies while giving birth to her second son, Benjamin, on the way to Ephrath (Bethlehem). Jacob sets up a memorial stone over her grave.

events.title: Joseph sold as a slave
events.description: Jacob's sons are jealous of Joseph because of his coat of many colors and the dreams in which the family bows down to him. They sell him to Midianite merchants who take him to Egypt, and they show Jacob the bloodstained robe.

events.title: Joseph interprets dreams in prison
events.description: Joseph ends up in prison after false accusations from Potiphar's wife. There he interprets the dreams of Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker. The cupbearer forgets Joseph for two years.

events.title: Pharaoh's Dream and Joseph as Leader
events.description: Pharaoh dreams of seven fat cows and seven lean cows, and seven full ears of grain and seven withered ones. Joseph interprets the dreams as seven years of abundance followed by seven years of famine. Pharaoh appoints Joseph to rule over all Egypt.

events.title: The Brothers Come to Egypt
events.description: Famine drives Jacob's sons to Egypt to buy grain. Joseph recognizes them but does not reveal himself. He tests them and demands that they bring Benjamin next time.

events.title: Joseph Reveals Himself
events.description: Joseph can no longer hold back his tears and reveals himself to his brothers. He says that God sent him ahead to preserve life. He asks them to bring Jacob and the whole family to Egypt.

events.title: Jacob Goes to Egypt
events.description: Jacob leaves with his entire family and travels to Egypt. God speaks to him in a vision at Beersheba and promises to make his descendants into a great nation there. Jacob and Joseph are reunited in Goshen after many years.

events.title: Jacob's Blessing over His Sons
events.description: The aging Jacob first blesses Joseph's sons Ephraim and Manasseh, placing the younger before the older. He then blesses all twelve of his sons with prophetic words about their future.

events.title: Jacob's Death and Burial
events.description: Jacob dies in Egypt and is embalmed. Joseph carries his father's body back to Canaan and buries him in the cave of Machpelah near Hebron, as Jacob had requested.

events.title: Joseph's Death
events.description: After Jacob's death, Joseph comforts his brothers and says: 'You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good.' Joseph dies at the age of 110 and is embalmed. He makes them swear to carry his bones to the promised land.
